# Rental market {#sec-rental}

## Rents climbed in every locality, with the sharpest gains since 2019


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Median gross rent rose in every Richmond-area locality between 2014 and 2024.](rental_files/figure-html/fig-median-rent-1.png){#fig-median-rent fig-align='left' fig-alt='Grouped horizontal bar chart of median gross rent for eight Richmond-area localities and Virginia in 2014, 2019, and 2024, in nominal dollars. Every locality\'s 2024 bar is well above its 2014 bar. New Kent has the highest 2024 median rent at $1,721 and Charles City the lowest at $1,099. Most of the increase occurs between 2019 and 2024.' width=100%}
:::
:::


- **Every locality posted a higher median gross rent in 2024 than in 2014, and in all eight the 2019-to-2024 increase outpaced the 2014-to-2019 increase.**
- New Kent had the region's highest 2024 median rent at $1,721; Charles City had the lowest at $1,099.
- Richmond city's median rent rose 54% over the decade, from $893 to $1,372 — yet stayed below the statewide median of $1,579.
- Small-county medians (New Kent, Powhatan, Goochland, Charles City) carry wide margins of error and describe small renter stocks; New Kent's 2014 estimate is Medium reliability (CV 15–30).
- All figures are nominal dollars; inflation-adjusted comparisons come with the cost-burden analysis.

## Renter households are growing again, led by Richmond city


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Renter shares held steady in the urban core while shrinking in most outer counties.](rental_files/figure-html/fig-renter-share-1.png){#fig-renter-share fig-align='left' fig-alt='Dumbbell chart comparing the renter share of households in 2014 and 2024 for eight Richmond-area localities and Virginia. Richmond city has by far the highest renter share, near 57 percent in both years. Henrico is near 36 percent in both years, and Virginia near 33 percent. The six remaining counties are all below 25 percent, and the smallest counties are lowest in 2024: New Kent and Powhatan each fell to about 7 percent.' width=100%}
:::
:::


- **The region added roughly 20,309 renter households between 2014 and 2024, a 15% increase.**
- Richmond city drove the gain, adding about 9,705 renter households — nearly half the regional increase — though its renter share held near 56% because total households grew just as fast.
- Chesterfield and Hanover renter counts grew steadily, but both counties remain more than three-quarters owner-occupied.
- The three smallest counties — Charles City, New Kent, and Powhatan — each had fewer renter households in 2024 than in 2014, deepening the ownership tilt of the outer region.
- Small-county renter counts are less precise: New Kent (2014 and 2024) and Powhatan (2024) estimates are Medium reliability (CV 15–30).

## Market asking rents surged after 2020 and are still rising, but at a third of the pandemic-era pace


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Regional average asking rent surged from 2020 through 2023 and has kept rising more slowly since.](rental_files/figure-html/fig-costar-rent-1.png){#fig-costar-rent fig-align='left' fig-alt='Line chart of the average multifamily asking rent per unit in the eight-locality Richmond region, quarterly from 2016 through mid-2026, in nominal dollars. The line rises gradually from about $1,100 in 2016 to $1,235 in early 2020, climbs steeply to roughly $1,480 by early 2023, and then keeps rising at a visibly flatter slope, ending at $1,583 in the second quarter of 2026.' width=100%}
:::
:::


- **Regional average asking rent reached $1,583 in 2026 Q2, up 44% from $1,096 in 2016 Q1.**
- Rent growth ran about 6% per year from 2020 to 2023, then slowed to roughly 2% per year — still rising, but at a third of the pandemic-era pace.
- Multifamily vacancy stood at 8.5% in 2026 Q2, up from a low near 5% in late 2021 as new deliveries caught up with demand.
- CoStar coverage is professionally managed multifamily; New Kent and Charles City have only a handful of tracked properties, so locality-level trends there are not meaningful.

::: {.callout-note}
## Since 2022
The 2022 Framework flagged a regional average asking rent of $1,395 in early 2022 as a two-decade high with vacancy near 5%. Rents have since risen another 11% to $1,583, but the market has loosened: vacancy is now 8.5%, and rent growth has slowed sharply. The 2022 Framework also reported a net *loss* of renter households from 2016 to 2020 (with a COVID-era data caveat); the 2020–2024 ACS instead shows renter households growing across the region.
:::
